purpose: Real result of dispatching .github/workflows/earnings-surprise.yml for the first time, for JBSS's own real filing (CIK 880117, accession 0001193125-25-256406) -- the same case already verified throughout Milestone 3's own work.
finding: SEC's data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyconcept/ endpoint returns HTTP 403 to this exact request (same CIK, same URL construction already verified correct via the built-in browser) from BOTH this Windows machine AND GitHub Actions' own infrastructure -- two separate, real dispatches, seconds apart, both blocked identically. This is a real, structural difference from every other data.sec.gov path this project has used (data.sec.gov/submissions/, used throughout Milestones 1-2, has worked reliably from GitHub Actions every time). Not a code bug: nre.ingestion.xbrl_company_concept() and the CLI command around it behave exactly as designed -- PublicClient.fetch() does not retry a 403 (by design, since 403 is not in its retryable set {429,500,502,503,504}, matching this project's own rule against bypassing bot-detection), and the failure surfaces cleanly as SourceUnavailable rather than crashing or fabricating a result.
what_was_verified_working: The identical XBRL data, at the identical URL, was successfully read through the built-in browser earlier in this same work (both when first designing nre/earnings_surprise.py and when building nre/ingestion.py's own real-data test fixtures) -- so the data itself, and this project's own understanding of its shape, are both confirmed correct. The gap is specifically automated (non-browser) programmatic access to this one API path.
not_attempted: No further retries beyond the two above, and no attempt to alter headers, timing, or request patterns to work around the block -- doing so would risk exactly the bot-detection-evasion this project's own standing rules (and Claude's own safety rules) prohibit. Two consistent, real failures are enough to characterize this as persistent rather than transient.

bulk_data_sets_path_checked_2026_09_30.what: SEC's own bulk 'Financial Statement Data Sets' (www.sec.gov/files/dera/data/financial-statement-data-sets/2025q4.zip -- quarterly ZIP archives of every registrant's own XBRL facts, published specifically for programmatic/bulk users, confirmed real and current via the page itself: coverage through 2026 Q2).
bulk_data_sets_path_checked_2026_09_30.local_result: HTTP 403 from this Windows machine via direct urllib, both with a bare request and with a full browser-equivalent header set (Accept, Accept-Encoding) added -- ruling out a simple missing-header cause, not just bot-detection avoidance.
bulk_data_sets_path_checked_2026_09_30.github_actions_result: A minimal, temporary HEAD-only probe workflow (.github/workflows/_diagnostic-bulk-sec-reachability.yml, deleted immediately after this result was recorded -- workflow run https://github.com/Fahad9101/NRE/actions/runs/36708611459) got HTTP_STATUS:403 from GitHub Actions' own infrastructure too.
bulk_data_sets_path_checked_2026_09_30.conclusion: This rules out the bulk-data path as an easy alternative. More importantly, it changes the diagnosis: the block is not specific to the XBRL companyconcept API path -- it now appears to affect multiple sec.gov paths (api/xbrl/companyconcept, and separately files/dera/data's own bulk download) from GitHub Actions' shared IP infrastructure, unlike data.sec.gov/submissions/ which has been reliable throughout. Building a pipeline against yet another SEC path is unlikely to fix this on its own without addressing that broader cause.

not_attempted_2: No attempt to spoof headers, rotate IPs/proxies, add delays to look 'more human', or any other measure aimed specifically at defeating SEC's own bot detection -- all of that would cross from 'sending a complete, standards-compliant request' into deliberate evasion, which this project's own rules and Claude's own safety rules both prohibit regardless of how sympathetic the reason.
not_a_claim: Not a claim that nre/earnings_surprise.py or nre/ingestion.py's own code is wrong -- both are tested and correct against real, verified data; this is purely an external access-path constraint.

Not a claim that these specific data sources are permanently unusable -- only that automated programmatic access to them is currently blocked from both this machine and GitHub Actions, unlike SEC's submissions/ endpoint this project already relies on successfully.

Not a claim that every SEC path beyond submissions/ is necessarily blocked -- only the two specifically tested here (api/xbrl/companyconcept/ and the bulk financial-statement-data-sets download) were confirmed blocked; this is not an exhaustive survey of SEC's own API surface.
